g1.correct: Cities are hotter than the countryside because of how they are built.
accept: Cities are hotter than the countryside because of how they are built.
g1.label: 1. Main idea of paragraph A
g1.why: The paragraph's point is the cause — “The reasons are built into the city itself”. The opening sentence only introduces the phenomenon, and waste heat is just one of the causes.

g2.correct: Street trees cool their surroundings in two ways.
accept: Street trees cool their surroundings in two ways.
g2.label: 2. Main idea of paragraph B
g2.why: “Trees fight the heat in two ways” is the point; planting numbers are an example and the slow growth of saplings is a detail.

g3.correct: Reflective surfaces stop heat being absorbed in the first place.
accept: Reflective surfaces stop heat being absorbed in the first place.
g3.label: 3. Main idea of paragraph C
g3.why: The paragraph argues for making surfaces “bounce sunlight back”; the Mediterranean towns are evidence and the cool-roof figures are a detail.

g4.correct: Cooling centres give people free, indoor relief from dangerous heat.
accept: Cooling centres give people free, indoor relief from dangerous heat.
g4.label: 4. Main idea of paragraph D
g4.why: The paragraph introduces cooling centres as free, air-conditioned public spaces; who they serve and the health checks are details.

g5.correct: Water cools city air as it evaporates.
accept: Water cools city air as it evaporates.
g5.label: 5. Main idea of paragraph E
g5.why: “Water is the oldest coolant of all” is the point; fountains and mist sprayers are examples, and the cost of stream projects is a detail.

g6.correct: The real challenge is making cooling reach the people who need it most.
accept: The real challenge is making cooling reach the people who need it most.
g6.label: 6. Main idea of paragraph F
g6.why: The final sentence states the point — reaching “the people who need them most”. Wealthy districts are an illustration and the budget problem is a detail.
